ResearchProjectDef.label: Jaffa weaponry
ResearchProjectDef.description: Study captured Jaffa weapon designs and adapt local machining techniques to reproduce Goa'uld energy weapons. Completed weapons recovered from the field remain usable before this research is finished.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Jaffa armor
ResearchProjectDef.description: Analyze modular Jaffa battlefield protection, including rank-marked command variants, and reproduce its layered armor components with local industrial materials. Captured armor remains wearable before this research is finished.

ResearchProjectDef.label: kara kesh
ResearchProjectDef.description: Reverse-engineer the naquadah-powered hand devices carried by Goa'uld System Lords, including their personal shield, focused kinetic blast and neural attack modes. Captured devices remain usable immediately, but reproducing one requires prior mastery of Jaffa armor construction.

ResearchProjectDef.label: SGC field equipment
ResearchProjectDef.description: Standardize local production of SG-team field clothing and modular mission equipment using established complex-clothing techniques. Equipment supplied by the stranded-team scenario remains usable immediately.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Goa'uld biotechnology
ResearchProjectDef.description: Adapt pharmaceutical and biological-production techniques to process Goa'uld symbiote material, prepare tretonin and construct specialized Prim'ta basins. Existing doses and larvae remain usable before this research is finished.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Goa'uld healing devices
ResearchProjectDef.description: Combine Goa'uld biotechnology with reverse-engineered naquadah interfaces to reproduce the compact healing bracelets carried by System Lords. Captured devices remain usable immediately.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Tok'ra secure communications
ResearchProjectDef.description: Decode the recognition lattice exposed by the recovered Tok'ra cipher module and adapt its protocols into a secure communications architecture. The physical module must first be analyzed at a research bench, and local electrical systems must be understood before formal research can begin.
